key_results: Curvature enhances H adsorption up to -6.87 eV; dipole moment up to 26.2 D; thermal stability under 10 keV proton beam (ΔT≤101 K); direct correlations between electronic properties and irradiation response
comments: Multiscale approach comprehensive but practical H-storage capacity and kinetic barriers not evaluated.

model_io.model: DFT calculations + PHITS Monte Carlo irradiation simulations

hypotheses.hypothesis: Curvature and external fields independently enhance H storage
hypotheses.result: Synergistic effects identified; quantitative correlations mapped between properties

title: Ultrafast many-body dynamics of dense Rydberg gases and ultracold plasma
task: Understanding ultrafast many-body dynamics in ultracold Rydberg gases vs ultracold plasmas
key_results: Femtosecond laser tuning controls initial state (Rydberg gas vs ultracold plasma); charge imbalance identified as primary decay driver; good agreement between MD simulations and experiments on electron distribution evolution
comments: Molecular dynamics validation thorough; detailed mechanisms of charge-imbalance-driven decay warrant deeper theoretical analysis.

model_io.model: Femtosecond laser excitation with molecular dynamics simulation

hypotheses.hypothesis: Rydberg blockade limits excitation density regardless of laser bandwidth
hypotheses.result: Femtosecond bandwidth overcomes blockade; charge imbalance becomes dominant decay mechanism

title: Global flux-driven turbulence simulations in chaotic plasmas
task: Global flux-driven turbulence simulation in reversed field pinch plasmas with magnetic chaos
key_results: Magnetic stochasticity exerts weak influence on turbulent transport in boundary region; radial electric field fundamentally altered by magnetic chaos; new perspective on ambipolar field formation in stochastic plasmas
comments: Self-consistent profile evolution provides valuable insight, though applicability beyond RFP requires validation.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Magnetic chaos significantly modifies turbulent transport mechanisms
hypotheses.result: Weak influence observed in boundary region; minor modifications in fluctuation statistics

title: Vortices and solitons in polariton superfluids and condensates
task: Controlling vortices and solitons in polariton superfluids and condensates
key_results: Review of polariton vortex/soliton formation with focus on spinor polaritons; half-integer topological charge vortices achievable; applications in quantum computing and all-optical circuits
comments: Comprehensive review but lacks discussion of experimental realization challenges and coherence requirements.

title: Symmetry-required orbital selectivity in monolayer FeSe
task: Identifying mechanism of orbital-selective correlations in monolayer FeSe
key_results: Symmetry-required orbital selectivity at M point: x²−y² orbitals strongly couple to antiferromagnetic fluctuations while {xz, yz} orbitals weakly couple; Fe-site localization of x²−y² states explains asymmetry
comments: Band-theory mechanism is elegant but limited to M-point analysis; generalizability to other Fe-based superconductors requires further validation.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Orbital selectivity arises from site-local Mott transition
hypotheses.result: Rejected; symmetry-protected band-structure mechanism at M point provides explanation
